name: Saddle Mountain Fire Lookout
summary: Saddle Mountain lookout near Nakusp, BC: wrecked by lightning in 1941 and struck again in 1943; the register dates the present lookout to 1963. Now a public trail to the summit.
design: Lookout building of the 1940s-60s type, per the heritage register
agency: Recreation Sites and Trails BC, with Nakusp And Area Community Trails Society

access.note: Public trail and recreation site. The lower section, hit by a 2018 windstorm and blowdown, is not currently maintained.

visit.trail_note: Drive to the upper parking lot and walk; the trail society suggests starting there. The trail is 5.3 km long and climbs an exposed outcrop to the lookout. Technical climbing is not required.

events.note: Forest Branch newsletter item dated November 10, 1939 names station VE9ES, picked up in Korea, as Saddle Mountain Lookout; the lookout was in use by then
Lightning bolt struck near the camp tent; the lookout building was moved off its foundation and generally wrecked
Eric Johansen was the lookoutman when a storm struck on the night of July 6. The year is taken from the October 20, 1941 newsletter item date
Second strike on August 26, 1943: tent frame demolished, tent partly burnt, radio antenna and mast destroyed (December 1943 item). A separate item calls the damage to the lookout negligible
Sam Jackson manned the lookout at the time of the 1943 strike
Register lists a home cabin built below the lookout for staff
Register lists the Fire Lookout (1963) among the features; the December 1943 item says the building had not been rebuilt by then, so the rebuild falls after 1943
Register lists a restoration by the Ministry of Forests, Recreation Sites and Trails in 2015 among the trail's upkeep
Windstorm and blowdown on the lower trail; the lower section is not currently maintained
